newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends lower, shakes off Colombia news.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends lower, shakes off Colombia news.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mainly weaker in choppy dealings on Wednesday, as traders brushed aside news of a threatened strike by Colombian dock workers, market sources said.
At one point during the session prices jumped some 3.00 cents a lb on the Colombia news, but the rally ran out of steam after operators discovered the work stoppage may be a far as a month away.
"It (the Colombia news) is worth some consideration but it won't be a factor until it comes up," said Smith Barney analyst Walt Spilka. "The market will react to it when it happens."

Most-active May rose to a peak of 171.80 cents before closing at 168.10 cents, down 0.70 cent on the day. May reached a low today of 165.50. July also fell 0.70, to 154.90, while the back months closed down 3.50 to up 2.90.

A union official said Wednesday dock workers at Buenaventura, Colombia's main Pacific coast port and the shipment point for 60 percent of the country's coffee exports, are threatening a strike which could begin in less than a month to protest port operators' failure to fulfill the terms of a January accord.
A nine-day dock workers' strike in January disrupted coffee exports from the world's second-largest producer and heightened supply concerns at a time when inventories were near 20-year lows.

New York futures surged to their highest level in two-and-a-half years two weeks ago on the supply crunch. But since then supply worries have eased as producers took advantage of higher prices and moved more coffee into exchange warehouses.

The CSCE reported late Wednesday certified coffee stocks grew for the tenth day in a row, reaching 64,529 60-kg bags as of March 18. There were an additional 17,100 bags pending grading, the exchange said.

"It is not a coincidence that as more supply started to come to market prices went down," said Spilka. He added, however, that continued uncertainty over the size of the 1997/98 Brazil crop as well as nervousness as Brazil approaches winter should underpin the market.
Traders will be keeping an eye on Thursday's Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) technical group meeting in London.
Although no major decision is expected, the meeting is expected to focus on the recent sharp hike in world coffee prices and its impact on consumption.
On the charts, May near-term support was seen at 165.50-165.00, then 160.00, traders said. Resistance in the May contract was pegged at 172.00, followed by 175.00-176.00.
Turnover was estimated at 9,000 lots, down sharply from Tuesday's official tally of 17,279 lots.
